what: One photo is split into three mask layers on a grid cell (276px at 1440 width, starting at 30 left·106 top). Each layer places the photo’s size and position slightly differently so the cells look like misaligned tiles, and while the element passes over the screen the layers shift by different amounts, −455.6/−364.5/−182.3px (at 1440). When the cover lifts, the layers rise from 250/200/100px below over 2.5 seconds to line up, and with two or more scenes it switches every 7 seconds — the outgoing layers go up, and the incoming scene appears .9s later over .9s with its layers rising from below

options.cell: Cell side (px, relative to base), default 276
options.base: Base width, default 1440 — cells and distances scale with element width
options.shift: Distance (px, comma-separated) the three layers shift on scroll, default ”455.6, 364.5, 182.3”
options.rise: Distances the three layers rise (px, comma-separated), default ”250, 200, 100”
options.spread: Multiplier of the size and position difference between layers, default 1 — at 0 they sit in the same place, so they don’t drift apart before scrolling
options.seed: Seed (integer) that distributes cells across layers, default 7
options.ratio: Photo ratio, default 1600 / 2600 (lays a portrait photo large at 145% width)
options.first: Seconds until the first change (from start of rising), default 4.6
options.start: ”load” makes it rise as soon as it is attached. By default it waits for an fx:play event on the element (when the cover lifts)
options.[data-fx-part=slide]: Scene — first child is a photo (also works as a placeholder). The part clones in three layers

use: …
note: The original masks are three hand-split SVGs, so the part draws cells of the same size split by a seed. Layer sizes and position table are values from the two original scenes (% of width)
